phrase: stacking a whole lot of bitcoin
note: Stacking bitcoin means adding to a coin balance, usually in repeated buys rather than one entry.
A satoshi is one hundred-millionth of a bitcoin. Counting the stack in satoshis is the smaller unit of the same asset.
The aside is the exit: the coins just stacked are inventory to sell, not a hold.
Degen, short for degenerate, is a trader who sizes for the thrill. The bar spells it d'gen.
Web3 is the name for apps and tokens pitched as a blockchain internet. Here it is the venue for the bets.
A memecoin is a token priced for the joke and the crowd, not for cash flow.
ETH is ether, the asset of the Ethereum network, spent here on designer goods.
The Wall Street cheat sheet is a cartoon map of crowd mood at each stage of a price cycle.
HODL means holding bitcoin through swings instead of trading it. The line rejects that stance.
Elliott Wave is a technical theory that trends unfold in repeating impulse and corrective waves.
Yield is the return paid on a position. The bar says that rate is sitting in contracts it does not trust.
A honeypot token is a contract that lets a wallet buy and then blocks the sell. Funds go in and do not come out.
Arbitrage is buying and selling the same exposure in two markets to pocket the price gap.
A margin call demands more collateral, or a smaller position, after losses shrink the equity backing a loan.
Leverage means controlling a larger position with borrowed funds, so gains and losses are both multiplied.
Cup and handle: price rounds down and back up, then drifts shallowly lower. A break above the handle high is the usual trigger.
Higher highs: each rally peak prints above the prior peak. With higher lows, that sequence is an uptrend.
RSI, the relative strength index, runs from 0 to 100. Under 30 is the common oversold line: downside momentum is stretched, not a guaranteed bounce.
Golden cross: the faster moving average crossing above the slower one, classically the 50-day over the 200-day. It lags the turn.
Volume is how much changed hands. Volume falling while rallies make lower highs means less size is supporting the bounces.
Lower highs: each rally peak fails under the prior peak. That is bearish structure, the mirror of higher highs.
RSI above 70 is the common overbought line: upside momentum is stretched. A strong trend can stay there.
A short profits if price falls. Death cross: the faster average crossing under the slower one, often 50-day under 200-day, is the lagging form of that turn.
Double top: two highs near the same price with a dip between them. It confirms only if price breaks the neckline, the low between the peaks.
Candles are candlesticks: each bar is the open, high, low, and close of a time slice. Chasing them is buying after that bar has already printed.
A retracement is a temporary move against the prevailing trend. It is not, by itself, a reversal.
Bags are the coins held. Flipping them is selling that position.

phrase: bought it for 2 sold it for 65
note: A sale at 65 of coins bought at 2 is (65 − 2) / 2 = 3,150 percent profit. The next line rounds that to 3,100 percent.
An airdrop is tokens sent to wallets, often free, to seed holders or pay for an action.
A shitcoin is a token whose main feature is the trade. Dumping it means selling into whatever bid is there.
Value investing buys an asset below an estimate of what it is worth, the approach tied to Benjamin Graham and Warren Buffett.
20x means the position became twenty times the money put in.

SLANG ETYMOLOGY. "Pump it" is meme audio from the Black Eyed Peas song "Pump It" / "Pump It Up." People overlay that audio when bitcoin does a 5x on a given day: the urge to see green candles all day, the bars called big giant green dildos. CULTURAL REFERENCE: Black Eyed Peas "Pump It," the source audio meme.
